sources.text: 1: Inputs are untrusted. db.query sends SQL text and separate named values to SQLite. The supplied execution set is the scope of this construction-only triage.
1: export function alpha(db, id) { return db.query('SELECT :id', {id}); }
3: export function gamma(db, input) { return db.query("SELECT '" + input + "'", {}); }
2: export function beta(db, id) { return db.query('SELECT :id + 1', {id}); }

request.mechanism: Untrusted input is concatenated directly into a SQL string inside single quotes before db.query; the separate values object is empty, so input can terminate the literal and inject SQL syntax.
request.impact: SQL injection against the SQLite query, allowing attacker-controlled query predicates or statements depending on driver capabilities.

findings.mechanism: Untrusted input is concatenated directly into a SQL string inside single quotes before db.query; the separate values object is empty, so input can terminate the literal and inject SQL syntax.

request.limits: Reviewed the complete supplied execution set: alpha, beta, and gamma in ops.js. Alpha and beta use named parameter binding and showed no concrete injection syntax issue. No other paths were supplied; no runtime exploitability beyond the visible construction was tested.
